# Testing {#sec-testing}

PhyloTrace is tested at two levels: `testthat` unit tests for the R code, and a
Cypress end-to-end test that drives the running app in a browser. This chapter
covers how the suite is organised, the pattern for testing `box` modules, the
database fixtures, and how to run it.

## The `testthat` suite {#sec-testing-unit}

Unit tests live in `tests/testthat`, one test file per script, named
`test-{script}.R`. Coverage is broad — nearly every logic module and every view
module has a corresponding test file, including the newer subsystems:

- **Data & schema** — `test-database_functions`, `test-db_events`, `test-db_store`,
  `test-db_sources`, `test-provenance`, `test-hash_database`.
- **Pipelines** — `test-pymlst`, `test-typing`, `test-mlst_repo`, `test-amr`,
  `test-genome_hash`.
- **Interoperability** — `test-db_compat`, `test-db_import`, `test-db_export`,
  `test-db_staging`, `test-profile_io`, `test-phylo_imported`,
  `test-database_transfer_modules`.
- **Visualization** — `test-mst_plot`, `test-tree_plot`, `test-epi_plot`,
  `test-amr_plot`, `test-mapping_engine`, `test-viz_export`, plus the view-level
  `test-visualization*`.

::: {.callout-important title="Why the logic/view split makes testing easy"}
`app/logic` holds Shiny-free code (@sec-arch-modules). That is what makes the
bulk of the suite possible: a distance kernel, a merge planner, a
matrix reshaper are all plain functions with inputs and outputs, so they are
tested directly — no browser, no reactivity to simulate. The view tests, which do
need Shiny, use `shiny::testServer` to exercise the reactive wiring.
:::

## Testing `box` modules {#sec-testing-box}

Because modules are `box` modules, tests import them the `box` way and reach
private functions through the module's namespace — the project convention
(`AGENTS.md`):

```{.r filename="tests/testthat/test-<module>.R"}
box::use(app/logic/mymodule)

# exported functions: via the module object
test_that("exported function works", {
  expect_equal(mymodule$exported_function(1), 2)
})

# non-exported functions: via the namespace attribute
impl <- attr(mymodule, "namespace")
test_that("internal helper works", {
  expect_true(impl$internal_function())
})
```

This tests both the public surface and the private helpers without breaking
encapsulation.

## Database fixtures {#sec-testing-fixtures}

Most tests need a realistic PhyloTrace database to run against. `helper-phylotrace-db.R`
builds one — a temporary `.db` with the pyMLST tables, metadata, and whatever
result tables a given test needs — so each test starts from a known, disposable
database rather than a shared mutable one. Static inputs live in
`tests/testthat/fixtures/`, and snapshot tests keep their expected output under
`tests/testthat/_snaps/` (compared with `testthat`'s snapshot mechanism, so a
change in rendered output is caught and reviewed rather than silently accepted).

## End-to-end tests {#sec-testing-e2e}

`tests/cypress/e2e/app.cy.js` is a Cypress spec that launches the app and drives
it through the browser — the check that the whole stack, not just the units,
holds together. It is the closest automated analogue to a user loading a
database, typing an isolate and drawing a plot.

## Running the tests {#sec-testing-run}

The R unit tests run through Rhino's test runner (which sets up the `box` module
paths), or directly with `testthat` against `tests/testthat`. The Cypress test
runs through the Rhino end-to-end tooling. Keeping the unit suite green is the
first gate for any change to a logic module; the one-test-file-per-script
convention makes it obvious which test to run for a given edit.

## Chapter summary

- `tests/testthat` holds one `test-{script}.R` per module, covering nearly the
  whole codebase; view tests use `shiny::testServer`.
- `box` modules are tested via the module object (exports) and the `namespace`
  attribute (privates).
- `helper-phylotrace-db.R` builds disposable database fixtures; `_snaps/` holds
  snapshot baselines.
- A Cypress spec (`app.cy.js`) drives the running app end-to-end.

The final operations chapter is how to add to the app safely — @sec-extending.
